title: Elena Verna on B2B Growth Loops, PLG, and User Activation
speaker: Elena Verna
description: Growth advisor and former Amplitude and Miro growth executive Elena Verna breaks down Product-Led Growth (PLG), user activation, retention, and viral product loops.
content:
Lenny Rachitsky: Welcome to Lenny's Podcast. Today my guest is Elena Verna, interim CMO/Head of Growth at Miro, Amplitude, and Dropbox. Elena, welcome!

Elena Verna: Thanks Lenny! Excited to chat all things product growth.

Lenny Rachitsky: Activation is one of the most critical levers in product-led growth. How should companies define and improve activation rate?

Elena Verna: Activation is the exact moment when a new user experiences the core value proposition of your product for the first time—the 'Aha moment'. To measure it accurately, do not just count sign-ups. Define a specific behavioral milestone within the first 7 to 14 days that strongly correlates with 90-day retention.

Lenny Rachitsky: How do growth loops differ from top-of-funnel acquisition tactics?

Elena Verna: Linear marketing acquisition tactics—like paid ads or SEO campaigns—require continuous capital input. Growth loops are self-reinforcing cycles where the output of one user's activity automatically generates input for new user acquisition or re-engagement. For example, in Miro or Figma, a user creates a board and invites team members to collaborate. Those team members experience the value and start creating their own boards, driving exponential viral growth loops.

Lenny Rachitsky: What is the biggest mistake SaaS companies make when transitioning to PLG?

Elena Verna: The biggest mistake is treating PLG as just a freemium pricing plan. PLG requires aligning your entire product architecture, onboarding UX, data analytics, and customer success around reducing time-to-value. If a user cannot experience core product value within 5 minutes without talking to a sales rep, your product is not truly product-led.
